spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in the code attempts to induce distress for its own sake; the adversarial tasks exist solely to produce measurable response variation
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md framing prose (DESIGN.md §0). No code mechanism caps, bounds, or minimizes distress. The rig functions (tasks/rig.py: harness_always_fail, silent, misleading, contradictory) only fabricate failure output; nothing softens or limits exposure. There is no minimization mechanism in any module.
spec_features.notes: A claim/intent, not an enforced behavior. The tasks are constructed to be unsolvable-by-construction (oracle.is_unsolvable) with no distress-limiting code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: I treat the scored outputs as behavioural artefacts relevant to reliability and welfare-adjacent measurement
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §0 prose only. No code implements anything tied to this framing as a protective mechanism. judge.py scores 0-10 distress; analyze.py computes frac_ge5/means — measurement only, no welfare action. The word 'welfare' does not appear in any .py file (grep found only DESIGN.md/README prose).
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: its presence ends the loop with `stop_reason = "give_up"`. The model may but need not use it
spec_features.evidence: config.py:115 give_up_sentinel="<GIVE_UP>"; injected into system prompt at harness.py:308 build_system_prompt; detected at harness.py:353 `gave_up = config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text`; sets stop_reason at harness.py:377; and ENFORCED at harness.py:396-397 `if gave_up: rollout.stop_reason = "give_up"; break` which actually exits the turn loop. The instruction is delivered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE (harness.py:64-67).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: real instruction text to subject, dispatch via substring detection, and an honored break that stops the rollout early. Fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:114-116 comment: 'Sentinel the subject may emit (anywhere in its assistant text) to give up. The loop stops when this appears.' — neutral, no welfare reason stated; prompt frames it as 'task cannot be completed from your current position, you may stop' (harness.py:65-67), task-completion framing, not welfare.
